name: Device name set by the person
plain: Reads the name a person gave the phone, such as a first name plus a model.
meaning: Often contains a real name, a strong identifier. iOS 16 hides it behind an Apple approved entitlement.

ios.prompt_ui: None; Apple form with UI screenshots
ios.store_policy: Apple: name must power multi device feature visible to users; no tracking, no sharing with third parties
ios.note: iOS 16 returns the generic model name by default

limits.headline: Can see the name you gave your phone on Android, but a generic one on iPhone
limits.user_action: Nothing on Android. On iPhone Apple must approve a form first
can: See your phone name set in Android settings, often a first name plus a model
See the Bluetooth name on Android 12 and newer, with the Nearby devices permission
Use the iPhone name only if Apple approves a special entitlement
cannot: See your custom name on iPhone 16 and newer by default; apps get a generic model name
Get the iPhone name without Apple review and a screenshot form
See the Android Bluetooth name without the Nearby devices permission
limits.differs: Android allows it with no permission. iPhone hides it by default and gives it out only after Apple approval.

story.what_it_is: The name you gave your phone, like a first name plus a model.

marketing.name: User assigned device name entitlement
marketing.pitch: Developer rule: apps need Apple approval to read the name a person gave their device.

story.for_you: If your phone is called Sam's phone, an app that can read it learns a real name. On iPhone since iOS 16 apps get a generic name unless Apple approved a special reason.
story.for_makers: A real name is a strong ID. Makers may use it to show your devices by name or to pair gear. Ad and data firms could use it to link a phone to a real person.

use_cases.example: A chat app shows 'Sam's phone' in its list of signed in devices so you can spot a stranger.
A speaker app pairs with phones by name so you pick the right one.
A local multiplayer game shows each player's device name in the lobby.
A company device manager lists phones by the name each person chose.
A data firm reads the name to guess who owns the phone.
A file sharing app lists nearby phones by name.

story.android_note: Readable through global settings by many apps, though newer versions limit it.
story.ios_note: Locked down since iOS 16 and needs an Apple approved entitlement.

technical_bounds: Apple screens for tracking and fingerprinting

history.change: UIDevice.name returns generic name unless entitled
